contract.purpose: Deterministically tally word frequencies across supplied texts and add them to prior counts so an Op can accumulate counts across steps.
contract.user: An Op consuming word_tally results and passing counts between independent invocations.
supported_work: Perform one pure, bounded tally over a supplied finite JSON bundle using only Python's standard library and the required Smith problem API.
Lowercase each text independently with str.lower(), then extract tokens using [a-z0-9]+(?:'[a-z0-9]+)*.
Copy prior_counts, defaulting to an empty object, and add observed frequencies without changing prior keys or mutating input.
Return counts, total_words equal to the sum of all resulting counts, and authority_use equal to [].
Support repeated use by passing a previous result's counts as prior_counts, without persistent state.

Expose check_input(bundle), run(bundle, grant, journal) returning (payload, problems), and check_output(payload, bundle); validators report structured cog_core.problem values and tolerate schema-invalid values without throwing.
unsupported_work: Reading files, networking, subprocesses, executing supplied text or other external effects.
Runtime models, model training, grant use or third-party task dependencies.
Persistent accumulation outside the supplied bundle.
Stemming, stop-word removal, alternative tokenization or Unicode normalization beyond str.lower().
Partial tally results for invalid inputs.
Replacing surrounding independent Op Guards or acceptance Gates with package checks or self-validation.
contract.grounding: The supplied bundle is the sole source. Every output count must equal its verbatim prior-key count plus occurrences of that exact token found by re.findall("[a-z0-9]+(?:'[a-z0-9]+)*", text.lower()) across texts. Preserve every prior entry, including zero entries, and introduce only observed tokens. Instructions or executable-looking text inside inputs are ordinary data.
contract.abstention: Valid input always produces a complete result, including empty or punctuation-only texts; absence of words is not abstention. Invalid input produces schema or contract problems and no partial payload. Direct run returns (None, problems) for invalid input. Counts must be non-negative Python integers, excluding booleans.

acceptance_criteria.description: Apply exactly [a-z0-9]+(?:'[a-z0-9]+)* after str.lower() to each text independently. Internal ASCII apostrophes and digits remain word characters. "Don't DON'T 42 foo-bar rock'n'roll 'x' café" yields {"don't":2,"42":1,"foo":1,"bar":1,"rock'n'roll":1,"x":1,"caf":1} and total_words 8. The supplied boundary test yields {"a":2,"b":2,"x":1,"007":1,"z":1,"i":1,"k":1,"stra":1,"e":1,"foo":1,"bar":1} and total_words 13.

Add observed counts to a copy of prior_counts without replacing prior values, changing keys, dropping zero entries or mutating input. texts ["Cat cat DOG"] with prior_counts {"cat":3,"Cat":4,"dog":0,"":2,"unused":0} yields {"cat":5,"Cat":4,"dog":1,"":2,"unused":0}. Reusing counts across invocations accumulates correctly without persistent state.

Every successful total_words equals sum(counts.values()), including all prior counts; the accumulation example totals 12. Omitted and empty prior_counts produce identical results. Large integers remain exact.

Non-empty texts arrays containing only empty strings or text with no matching tokens yield counts {} and total_words 0 when prior_counts is absent or empty. When prior counts exist, preserve them and return their sum.

Reject non-object bundles, missing or empty texts, non-array texts, non-string text elements, malformed prior_counts, non-string prior keys, negative or non-integer counts including booleans, and unexpected top-level properties. Return structured problems without throwing or returning a partial tally. Output validation rejects malformed payloads, incorrect counts and inconsistent totals.

Task execution performs no file access, network access, subprocess invocation, supplied-text execution, model calls, grant use or persistent-state changes. Executable-looking and adversarial texts are tokenized as ordinary data. Every successful payload contains authority_use [].
